title: Trade-history/ledger table + realized-loss-aware 6% Rule -- non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #148 (backend-trade-history-table), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: New tests in backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_delete_position.py (test_records_closed_trade_with_default_unspecified_exit_reason, line ~168) and backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_risk.py (TestRealizedLossesThisMonth, lines ~609/657/695) assert against local `date.today()`-derived fixtures/expectations, but the production code that sets/queries the exact same dates (`app.api.routers.portfolio._today()`) is explicitly `datetime.now(UTC).date()`-based, matching every other 'now' helper in this codebase (app.data.cache._utcnow, app.api.routers.watchlist._utcnow). On a machine/CI runner whose local timezone isn't UTC, any run occurring in the local-date-vs-UTC-date skew window (e.g. local UTC-8, any time between local midnight and UTC midnight) makes `trade.exit_date` (UTC-derived) differ from the test's local `date.today()`, failing the exit_date assertion intermittently -- and near a calendar-month boundary, the `this_month`/`last_day_of_prior_month` fixture construction in test_portfolio_risk.py could put a ClosedTradeORM row in the wrong bucket relative to what `_realized_losses_this_month_pct`'s UTC `as_of` actually uses. Currently harmless (dev container and CI both run in UTC per `/etc/timezone`), but the tests should build their expectations from `datetime.now(UTC).date()` (or freeze time) rather than local `date.today()`, for the same reason every other UTC-'now' helper's own tests already do.

frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/RiskSummaryCard.tsx and RiskPanel.tsx's 'Total Open Risk' StatCard label now silently displays a combined open-risk + this-month's-realized-losses figure with no copy change -- deliberately deferred per this task's own `decisions` entry (scoped backend-only; real UI work better paired with the future trade-journal frontend task where the two components can be shown separately). Tracked here so the deferred copy/breakdown work isn't forgotten: a user who took realized losses earlier this month but holds only low-risk open positions currently sees a misleadingly-labeled 'Total Open Risk' figure that could lead them to trim healthy open positions instead of addressing the real (already-realized) cause.

frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.test.tsx (lines ~69, ~94) and frontend/src/pages/PortfolioPage.test.tsx (line ~58) build RiskResponse MSW fixtures that were not updated to include the new required `realized_losses_this_month_pct` field, unlike every other RiskResponse fixture this PR touched (RiskPanel.test.tsx, RiskSummaryCard.test.tsx, SellFlaggedPositionsCard.test.tsx, frontend/tests/mocks/handlers.ts). Currently harmless -- `HttpResponse.json()` isn't type-checked against `RiskResponse` here and no component under test reads the new field yet -- but it's an inconsistency within this PR's own diff, and the gap would surface as a silent `undefined` (not a compiler/test failure) the moment a future change makes a component read `realized_losses_this_month_pct` (e.g. the label/breakdown follow-up above). Add the field to both fixtures for consistency and future-safety.

decisions.decision: Fixed the timezone-mismatch test fixtures (checklist item 1) by adding a local `_today()` helper to both backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_delete_position.py and backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_risk.py, defined identically to `app.api.routers.portfolio._today()` (`datetime.now(UTC).date()`), and replacing every local `date.today()` call in those two files with it. Did not adopt freezegun/time-freezing (an alternative considered): these are integration tests exercising the real DELETE/GET-risk request/response cycle end to end, where the specific real 'today' value doesn't matter to what's being verified (only that the test's expectation and the production code agree on what 'today' means) -- a small matching helper achieves that with zero new dependency, mirroring the exact pattern `tests/unit/data/test_cache.py`'s own local `_now()` helper already uses for the same underlying problem (matching `app.data.cache._utcnow`).
decisions.rationale: The point of the original review finding was that the test's own date source diverged from the production code's date source (local vs. UTC), not that the tests needed a deterministic/frozen clock -- matching the two sources of 'now' (both UTC-derived) closes that gap directly without introducing time-freezing machinery this codebase doesn't otherwise use anywhere. freezegun/monkeypatching `datetime.now` was rejected as unnecessary weight for a fix that's really about parity, not determinism.

decisions.decision: Fixed the misleading 'Total Open Risk' label (checklist item 2) by renaming the StatCard label itself to 'Total Risk (Open + Realized)' in both RiskSummaryCard.tsx and RiskPanel.tsx, and adding a `common/MetricHelp` question-mark icon (StatCard's existing `corner` slot, same pattern as IndicatorsPanel.tsx) that explains the two-part 6% Rule and shows a concrete numeric breakdown (open-position-risk-portion vs. this-month's-realized-losses-portion, recovered as `total_open_risk_pct - realized_losses_this_month_pct` since the backend only exposes the combined total plus the realized-losses half). The breakdown content lives in a new small shared helper, frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/totalRiskHelp.ts, rather than either duplicating the MetricHelp copy inline in both components or adding a new entry to features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts's registry (that registry is stocks-page-scoped and its content is keyed to stock-analysis metrics, not portfolio-risk ones). Also updated both components' 6%-rule breach banner text ('total open risk is X%' -> 'total risk (open positions plus this month's realized losses) is X%') for the same accuracy reason, since it renders the identical combined figure right next to the StatCard. Did NOT split the combined figure into two separate StatCards/components (the fuller breakdown UI the original PR's decisions entry explicitly deferred to a future trade-journal-adjacent task) -- frontend-trade-journal (PR #150, already merged) added a separate TradeJournalPanel but never touched RiskSummaryCard/RiskPanel, so that deferred split still doesn't exist; a full redesign remains out of scope for this non-blocking copy-accuracy follow-up.
decisions.rationale: A rename-only fix (no breakdown at all) would satisfy the letter of 'accurately reflect what it now shows' but not the review's actual concern -- a user still couldn't tell how much of the number came from open risk vs. already-realized losses, which is exactly the scenario (trimming healthy positions instead of addressing realized losses) the original finding warned about. A full two-StatCard split was rejected as over-scope for a tracked non-blocking follow-up (it would re-litigate the original PR's own deliberate, well-reasoned deferral without new information justifying revisiting it, and duplicate work the trade-journal task was supposed to own). The chosen middle ground -- accurate label + an on-demand breakdown via the same MetricHelp affordance already used elsewhere in this app for exactly this kind of 'what does this number mean' explanation -- fixes the actual misleading-copy problem with a small, low-risk, precedented change. Label wording ('Total Risk (Open + Realized)' over alternatives like 'Total Portfolio Risk' or '6% Rule Total') was chosen to name both components explicitly rather than requiring the reader to already know the 6% Rule's two-part definition.
decisions.note: StatCard label/copy changes rippled into: RiskPanel.test.tsx, RiskSummaryCard.test.tsx, DashboardPage.test.tsx, PortfolioPage.test.tsx (text-match assertions), tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts, tests/e2e/portfolio.spec.ts (Playwright text assertions) -- all updated to match, and the full frontend test suite plus the persisted e2e suite (`make e2e`, 16/16 specs) were re-run and pass. frontend/src/components/common/StatCard/StatCard.stories.tsx's own 'Total Open Risk' label was deliberately left as-is: it's a generic illustrative example of StatCard's `delta` prop in isolation, unconnected to any real risk-response data, not a claim about what the real feature currently shows.

decisions.decision: For checklist item 3, added `realized_losses_this_month_pct` to the three RiskResponse fixtures in DashboardPage.test.tsx (2 occurrences) and PortfolioPage.test.tsx (1 occurrence) that were missing it, matching every other RiskResponse fixture in the codebase. Confirmed via grep that neither test file imports or type-annotates its `HttpResponse.json(...)` payload against the `RiskResponse` type (msw's `HttpResponse.json` isn't generic here) -- so this genuinely was, as the original review noted, an incomplete-but-currently-harmless fixture gap, not a live type-safety hole tsc was silently missing. Fixed anyway per the checklist's own instruction ('for consistency and future-safety'), not because tsc needed it.
decisions.rationale: Confirming the 'genuine gap vs. harmless fixture' question empirically (grep for RiskResponse imports in both files, re-running `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` clean before and after) rather than assuming either way, per the dispatch instructions' own framing of this as something to verify rather than take at face value.
